pages.title: What Paykit does
pages.description: Understand payment coordination, then run a safe local wallet or point-of-sale demo.

sections.title: Coordinate a payment, not custody it
paragraphs: Paykit helps applications discover how a counterparty can receive payment and exchange payment-related messages over Pubky. A payment endpoint pairs an endpoint-type identifier with its receiving-detail payload; a rail is the payment system your application uses to act on it.

Paykit is not a wallet balance or settlement service. Your application retains funds, user authorization, rail execution and settlement checks. Start with a local demo before adding identity, storage or network access.

sections.title: Choose the integration surface
list: paykit-lib: validated values, app-scoped public discovery and private protocol helpers. You manage sessions and durable state when using this layer directly.
paykit-sdk: a stateful Rust runtime with storage, live-session and payment-adapter boundaries. Prefer this for a durable application rather than rebuilding request and link state.

paykit-ffi: Paykit uses UniFFI to generate bindings so Swift and Kotlin apps can call the Rust SDK. Binding availability is separate from a Rust crate version; the local Rust demos below do not exercise mobile bindings.

sections.title: Use one source snapshot
paragraphs: These development pages use the source-tagged prerelease v0.1.1-rc9 at commit 0b9c63d25dbd0cd5e7cf6ec577bc170732d350be. The paykit-lib, paykit-sdk and paykit-ffi manifests all declare 0.1.1-rc9. The tutorials use an exact Git revision, not a floating branch. A source tag does not establish registry-package or generated mobile-binding availability.

sections.title: From a demo to an application

Point-of-sale outcome: build valid request terms and round-trip the request through serialization and parsing.
Before network work: review public versus private data, authenticated peer keys, shared-state requirements and app-owned payment checks.

pages.title: Components and relationships
pages.description: Choose the library, stateful runtime and application adapters without confusing them with a payment rail.

sections.title: How the layers fit
paragraphs: The SDK adds durable coordination around the library. Pubky supplies the network/storage backend; the payment rail is a separate application integration.

diagram.caption: A Rust integration layers durable SDK state over the lower-level Pubky helpers.
diagram.alt: Your application constructs paykit-sdk with storage, session and payment adapters. The SDK uses paykit-lib. The library reads and writes Pubky storage. Payment-rail execution is outside this stack.

sections.title: Supply three application boundaries
list: StorageAdapter: commits SDK mutations atomically and preserves ordering. Apps sharing a Pubky identity must share the same logical durable state.
PubkySessionProvider: exposes current authenticated Pubky access from your app or platform. It is not a secure credential store or a user sign-in screen.
PaymentAdapter: supplies receiving details, candidate selection and payment targets. It does not execute payments or validate settlement for you.
paragraphs: For live private communication, supply live Pubky access and matching identity-wide Paykit key material. An app-owned App ID provides attribution within that identity, not a new identity.

Atomicity applies to each storage transaction, not the whole multi-transaction operation: later failure does not roll back earlier commits. A storage operation must not call SDK methods or wait on spawned tasks that access the same storage. Session creation, persistence, capability renewal and identity-wide key distribution remain application responsibilities.

Your public receiving-details callback returns the complete desired endpoint set. Empty results remove every SDK-managed endpoint; a subset removes omitted endpoints. If a receiving backend is not ready, return an error rather than an empty or partial set.

App enrollment is explicit: publish_paykit_app adds or replaces the configured app in the identity-wide registry and requires an active Pubky session. In RC9, initial identity refresh and publication share one SDK storage operation; the per-transaction failure rules above still apply. Restore a backup before publishing, not afterwards.

links.label: Identity and App ID: the live private-communication prerequisite

sections.title: App ownership is not private isolation
paragraphs: A Paykit App ID identifies which app owns a public endpoint and attributes private messages. Public endpoints live under /pub/paykit/v0/apps/{app_id}/endpoints/. Do not place secrets or private order details there.

Apps on one identity share private communication and state; an App ID is not a cryptographic boundary between mutually authorized apps. Private links require signed Noise key authorization, not just a key advertised in a public registry. The SDK checks peer authorization pins and authenticated static keys.

links.label: Read the trust and deployment constraints

sections.title: Rust first, bindings separately
paragraphs: The tutorials use paykit-lib to expose a small protocol outcome. A stateful Rust app can integrate paykit-sdk for durable coordination workflows. Swift/Kotlin integrations use the source-matched FFI surface; these pages do not claim a tested mobile build.

In RC9, Pubky clients created by the bindings send identity-record requests over HTTP to a PKARR relay, including on local testnets. The relay accesses the DHT, the network for those records, so the client does not connect to it directly. When publishing a record, the client still waits for the relay.

sections.title: Implemented in the v0.1.1-rc9 snapshot
paragraphs: The SDK includes read_payment_requests, which checks live identity status and reads one counterparty's request records in a bounded storage operation when live access is available. It checks the optional expected identity; without live access it reads only locally available identity metadata and returns no request records. The upstream signed-out test covers that empty-record behavior.

This read does not authorize payment or make later proof submission idempotent. Do not cache its result for payment checks or reuse it across a mutation. Earlier transaction commits survive a later error; only the documented outer-lock SharedStateBusy acquisition failure is a safe retry point, not every failure. This helper is not used by the local demos and is not a claim about the released API.

For receipt history, issued_receipt reads and decrypts a locally issued receipt, including metadata, before Receipt Access delivery. Another app sharing the identity can read it; missing records return NotFound and blocked counterparties return Policy. This is local SDK state access, not proof that a peer received the receipt or that payment settled.

Receipt issuance views derive AccessSent and AccessFailed from the matching outbound Receipt Access message; the durable issuance record remains AccessQueued. The FFI exposes these statuses and delivery-aware updated_at and last_error fields. These are source-inspected SDK/binding behaviors, not mobile or network tests performed by these tutorials.
list: RC9 profile routing: fetch_pubky_profile prefers /pub/social/v1/profile.json and tries the legacy pubky.app profile only when it is absent, not after a read error. Profile publication follows the identity's migration flag. Apps editing the shared profile must add PUBKY_APP_PROFILE_SESSION_CAPABILITIES, including migration-flag read access; these are separate from Paykit session scopes.

RC9 reservation-backed list sync: after restart, an unchanged list with the same unexpired reservations can reuse its sent outbound record when the peer is Linked, stored link state still matches, and the send was more than five minutes after the peer's last link change or private receive. Otherwise the list is republished once. Timestamp-based reuse alone is not reported in acknowledged: this runtime did not witness that publication.

pages.title: A payment interaction
pages.description: Separate public discovery, private request coordination and application-owned execution.

sections.title: 1. Discover receiving details
paragraphs: For public discovery, the payee publishes app-scoped receiving details and the payer reads that app's PaymentList. The endpoint identifier says which method the payload describes; the payload wrapper does not validate an invoice or make it payable.
The payer must support the method and apply its own selection and risk policy. The wallet demo demonstrates only this local map lookup, including the no-shared-rail case.

diagram.caption: Public discovery finds receiving details; it does not send a payment.
diagram.alt: The payee app publishes app-scoped endpoint text to public Pubky storage. The payer reads the endpoint list for that payee and app. Payer-owned policy selects a supported rail; reading or selecting an endpoint does not execute that rail.

sections.title: 2. Exchange and review request terms
paragraphs: For request-based coordination, establish an authorized Encrypted Link first. The payee proposes an amount, asset, reference and accepted payment methods. The payer reviews the request and can accept or reject it; low-level callers must enforce the sender roles.
Only the application can authorize a financial action. Its rail integration executes the payment and checks the outcome. The point-of-sale demo stops before sending any private message.

links.label: Try a local request round trip

diagram.caption: A private request coordinates terms. Authorization, rail execution and settlement checks belong to the application.
diagram.alt: The payee sends typed request terms to the payer on an Encrypted Link. The payer application reviews and authorizes the payment before its own rail code executes it. The application verifies the rail outcome before deciding settlement; Paykit request acceptance and proof messages are not that verification.

sections.title: 3. Track coordination without inventing settlement
list: Accepted means acceptance is recorded locally, not that funds moved.
ProofSubmitted means a one-time proof is present in local history. Validate method-specific evidence and the actual rail result before marking an order paid.

A queued proposal is local intent, not confirmed delivery. Persist the request ID, counterparty and exact original terms before proposing; retry with propose_payment_request_with_id as the same creating App and identity while retaining that identity's proposal/Event Message history.

Proposal idempotency depends on retained shared Event Message history, not a permanent independent ID registry. Deleting state or restoring a backup from before creation loses that protection; reconcile external order and execution records before recreating a request or executing payment.

AccessSent means Receipt Access was published, not that the peer read it. AccessFailed means delivery stopped without automatic retry because the outbound message is invalid or the link needs recovery. A retryable delivery error may leave AccessQueued with last_error set. None of these statuses verifies settlement.

sections.title: Keep failure paths explicit
paragraphs: Public and private resolution are separate paths. A missing or recovering private link is not permission to expose a private payment through a public fallback. Request-bound endpoints further constrain the permitted destination; do not silently replace them.

Your app decides when a private list has been used. Before submitting a payment that uses up the list, save its version from the payable result (private_payment_list_version). Next time you look up the same peer in the same SDK state, pass that value as after_private_payment_list_version. WaitingForUpdatedPaymentList means the SDK found no newer list and returned no payable endpoints. Wait for new details; do not resend the payment or switch to public discovery.

For received requests, resolve_public_payment_request returns Policy for a blocked counterparty and rechecks the block around public-provider and adapter calls. Plain resolve_public_contact_payment deliberately ignores Linked Peer state. Calls already in flight are not recalled, and reads inside one App's Payment List are not interrupted; do not treat this as cancellation of every public read.

links.label: Rust SDK: how to check for newer private payment details

pages.title: Responsibilities, trust and limitations
pages.description: Know what a local success proves and what remains your application or deployment responsibility.

sections.title: What Paykit handles; what you must handle
list: Paykit: validated protocol values, endpoint discovery, typed message encoding/decoding and SDK state coordination.
Your application: consent and authorization, funds and balances, invoice/target interpretation, fees, route policy, execution and independent settlement checks.
A parsed request, a delivery event or a receipt is coordination evidence, not a substitute for rail-specific proof validation.

sections.title: Public data and private trust
paragraphs: Public endpoint payloads are public text. Private message raw_json and SDK backup/state exports are sensitive plaintext in the application, even when the transport or live shared-state resource is encrypted. Keep them out of logs and protect exported backups.

Use identity-signed Noise key authorization and retained peer pins for private links. Registry metadata alone is not that authorization. App IDs scope ownership, not mutual trust; apps with shared identity keys and write access share private state.
Live-state encryption does not conceal resource existence, size or update timing, and does not prevent homeserver replay.

sections.title: A production shared-state prerequisite
paragraphs: For Paykit shared state, verify that every serving homeserver runs version 0.16.2 or newer and uses the GCS object-storage backend, not filesystem storage. Paykit does not check the server version or storage backend for you. Upgrading the Rust dependency or seeing WebDAV-lock support does not establish compatibility.

All participating writers must use lock tokens and pre-upgrade writes must be drained before rollout. Separate device-local blobs do not satisfy the shared-identity contract. Failed or unconfirmed state publication can leave recovery pending; never replace a failed load with empty state just to proceed.

links.label: Paykit SDK: which homeserver version and storage backend to verify

sections.title: What these tutorials do not establish
list: The wallet demo uses an in-memory endpoint map, not live discovery. Its payload is deliberately not a payable invoice.
The point-of-sale demo validates and parses local terms. It opens no encrypted link, negotiates no conversion and settles no order.
Decimal/asset syntax validation does not establish asset precision, an exchange rate, economic correctness or counterparty capability.

The pinned implementation and test sources were inspected, not executed for this refresh. No SDK, demo, mobile-binding or live-network run is claimed; these pages are not a security audit or proof of your deployment.

sections.title: Separate a proposal from implemented behavior
paragraphs: The specs/v0.2 folder is a review candidate for a redesigned transport and coordination model. Its README says the design is not frozen, adds no code and leaves v0.1 as the current protocol.
Do not read those proposed guarantees into this development snapshot. The source-pinned demos and the implemented SDK remain the basis of these pages; there is no shipping promise for the redesign.

pages.title: Wallet: select a supported rail
pages.description: Choose a known endpoint type from an in-memory PaymentList and handle an unsupported method without sending a payment.

sections.title: What the local demo shows
paragraphs: Choose a known endpoint type from an in-memory PaymentList and handle an unsupported method without sending a payment.
Use no real funds, production credentials or live payment targets. Building may download toolchain and dependency files; running this demo makes no Pubky discovery request and sends no payment.

sections.title: 1. Prepare and download the demo
list: Install Rust through rustup so the included rust-toolchain.toml can select Rust 1.91.1. The shell commands below assume a terminal with tar.
Have a C compiler/linker, pkg-config and internet access for toolchain/dependency downloads and the pinned Git source.
Start in an empty working directory. Use the link below to download the archive into that directory; keep its filename unchanged.

links.label: Download the wallet demo for this version

sections.title: 2. Extract and run
paragraphs: The archive contains Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml and src/main.rs; no separately copied code is needed.

The manifest pins paykit-lib to Git revision 0b9c63d25dbd0cd5e7cf6ec577bc170732d350be, the source selected for v0.1.1-rc9. Keep this exact source pin rather than substituting a registry dependency or floating branch.
Run these commands in order from the directory holding the downloaded archive. Keep Cargo.lock and use --locked; the toolchain file selects the pinned compiler.

code.code:
tar -xzf paykit-wallet-coming-soon.tar.gz
cd paykit-wallet-demo
cargo run --locked
code.caption: Run the downloaded demo.

sections.title: 3. Read the dependency and the demo code
paragraphs: The choose function is application-owned selection policy, not an automatic Paykit rail selector. It checks a known method against the local map, asserts no match for an unsupported rail, and rejects an unsafe identifier.

code.caption: Exact dependency source for this snapshot.
code.code:
[package]
name = "paykit-wallet-demo"
version = "0.0.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.91.1"

[workspace]
resolver = "3"

[dependencies]
paykit-lib = { git = "https://github.com/pubky/paykit-rs", rev = "0b9c63d25dbd0cd5e7cf6ec577bc170732d350be" }

code.caption: Complete local demo; no network integration is opened.

sections.title: 4. Check the result
paragraphs: This is the expected result when you run the demo, not an execution report from this refresh. A successful run should exit with status 0 after all assertions pass. Cargo may print download or compilation messages separately; expected program stdout is:

code.code:
demo-pos: shared rail btc-lightning-bolt11; unsupported rail: no shared rail
Local fixture only; no discovery request or payment was sent.
code.caption: Expected program stdout.

sections.title: What this success proves
list: Validated identifiers and the endpoint map are usable with this exact dependency.
Your small selection policy finds the advertised known method and returns no shared rail for the unsupported one.
It does not prove network discovery, invoice validity, available liquidity, an authenticated private session or settlement.

sections.title: If the result differs
list: tar reports a missing file: download this version's archive first, keep its filename unchanged and run extraction from the download directory.
cargo or rustup is missing, or Rust 1.91.1 cannot be selected: install/repair rustup, then rerun inside the extracted directory so rust-toolchain.toml is discovered.
A compiler, linker or pkg-config error appears: install the missing build prerequisite. A dependency or toolchain download error needs working network access, not payment credentials.
Cargo says the lock file needs updating: use a fresh extraction and cargo run --locked. Do not delete the lock, loosen the version or switch to a floating branch to make the demo pass.
No shared rail in your own data: compare the exact endpoint identifiers with your supported set. A wrapped payload is not proof that your backend can pay it.
An assertion fails or stdout differs: retain the error and the archive version, then retry a clean extraction. Do not supply real funds or credentials to repair a local demo.

If a clean extraction repeats the problem, use the linked public upstream issue tracker to report a minimal reproduction. Identify this documentation page and its demo archive URL/version, the exact error and expected result, Rust/Cargo versions, and operating system/architecture. Say whether you suspect an upstream library problem or a documentation or demo packaging problem; do not assume upstream owns this archive or guarantees support. Share only non-sensitive diagnostics: remove keys, session/auth material, backups, private messages, endpoint payloads and payment secrets.

links.label: Report a repeatable problem: upstream Paykit issue tracker

sections.title: Next: replace the demo with real discovery
list: Direct read-only lookup with paykit-lib: call get_payment_list with the PublicStorage handle from your Pubky client (public_storage()), the payee’s Pubky public key, and the App ID of the app that published the receiving details under that key. Keep client timeouts and fetch budgets explicit.

If you only have the payee’s Pubky public key, call `get_paykit_app_registry` with `PublicStorage` and that key to see registered App IDs before your app chooses which App ID to pass to `get_payment_list`. The registry may be absent or list several apps; a registration or default doesn’t guarantee a usable endpoint.

Durable resolution with paykit-sdk: use resolve_public_contact_payment for the payee's public endpoints or resolve_private_contact_payment for private lists. Keep that choice explicit: private failure is not public fallback permission.

Publish your own app and public endpoints: construct paykit-sdk with shared storage, a live-session provider and your payment adapter. Restore any backup before app publication. Enroll the app with publish_paykit_app; sync_public_endpoints publishes your adapter's receiving details.

Replace the demo payload and lookup policy with rail-specific target validation, user authorization, durable execution intent and settlement checks. Verify shared-state deployment requirements before multi-app use.

links.label: Public payment lookup: get_payment_list example and inputs

sections.title: Non-production SDK integration checklist
list: Use paykit-sdk with live Pubky access, durable shared state and a payment adapter. Restore any backup before app publication. Publish identity-signed Noise key authorization before publishing private app capabilities with publish_paykit_app. If your Rust app initiates a new encrypted link, call initiate_link_with_peer with the counterparty’s Pubky public key (PubkyPublicKey), not an App ID or a Noise key. For that same peer, use advance_link_handshake to advance the Rust handshake. A successful report with state LinkedPeerState::Linked means the handshake is complete locally; Linking means it’s still in progress. If your app drives the handshake manually and a successful report still says `Linking`, call `advance_link_handshake` again for the same peer on your app’s next poll. Link completion does not mean a request was delivered.

Persist the order reference, exact terms, counterparty and a newly generated request ID before proposing. Retry propose_payment_request_with_id only as the same creating App and identity with the same values and retained shared Event Message history. After state deletion or a pre-creation backup restore, reconcile order and execution records first; the saved ID alone does not prevent duplicates. Never reuse the demo's fixed ID across real orders.
Define your own asset precision and conversion policy. The example usd amount and Lightning method do not establish conversion support or a payable destination.

Track local queue and request state separately from delivery and payment state. The payer uses request-constrained resolution; acceptance or ProofSubmitted is not permission for the merchant to release goods.
Bind method-specific proof to the order and request, and independently validate the rail outcome before marking an order paid.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.description: Key terms for reading this version's wallet, point-of-sale and payment-coordination guides.

sections.title: Accepted
paragraphs: The SDK request state indicating that an acceptance is recorded in local history. It can appear while the acceptance message is still queued; it does not establish peer delivery or that a payment happened.

sections.title: App ID
paragraphs: An identifier for an application within a Paykit identity, used to attribute public endpoints and private messages. It does not create a separate identity, Encrypted Link or private trust boundary.

links.label: Define identity before choosing an App ID
Understand app ownership and shared identity

sections.title: Encrypted Link
paragraphs: The private connection used to exchange Paykit application messages with a counterparty through pubky-noise. SDK links rely on identity-signed Noise key authorization, retained peer pins and authenticated static-key checks, not unsigned key fields in the public App Registry.

sections.title: Endpoint payload
paragraphs: The UTF-8 receiving-detail text carried by a payment endpoint, such as an address, invoice or JSON descriptor. The payload wrapper stores text; it does not establish that the details are payable, so the application or payment adapter must interpret and validate them.

links.label: Discover receiving details without executing payment

sections.title: Event ID
paragraphs: A UUID-v4 identifier for one Event Message. A request proposal carries both an Event ID for that message and a Payment Request ID for the request.

links.label: See the request and event identifiers in the local demo

sections.title: Idempotent proposal
paragraphs: Queuing a request with propose_payment_request_with_id lets a matching retry return the original proposal without queuing a second one. Persist the ID, counterparty and exact terms first, and retry as the same creating app and identity with retained Event Message history; deleting state or restoring a backup from before creation loses this protection. Every call still requires current session, app-capability and link checks; success describes the local queue, not payment authorization or confirmed delivery.

links.label: Plan durable request creation and retries

sections.title: Identity
paragraphs: Here, a Paykit identity is the shared Paykit context of a Pubky public-key identity: its apps share private links and SDK state. An App ID names an application within that context, not a new identity. Establishing or advancing Encrypted Links requires live authenticated Pubky access and matching identity-wide Paykit key material. The Paykit secret is derived from the Pubky secret and may be supplied separately to delegated apps; it is not the Pubky secret itself.

links.label: Understand app ownership without private isolation

sections.title: Issued receipt
paragraphs: A receipt prepared by the local identity that the SDK can decrypt from its issuance state, including metadata, even before Receipt Access delivery. Another app sharing the identity can read it; blocked counterparties and missing records are rejected. This local read proves neither peer receipt nor settlement.

sections.title: Payment adapter
paragraphs: The application-supplied SDK boundary for method-specific receiving details, endpoint selection and payment-target construction. Financial execution, proof validation and settlement checks remain application or adapter responsibilities rather than SDK outcomes. Public receiving details are the complete desired set: an empty or partial result removes omitted SDK-managed endpoints, so return an error if a receiving backend is unavailable.

sections.title: Payment amount
paragraphs: A decimal value expressed as text together with an asset name. Paykit checks their syntax but defines no asset registry or precision policy; applications still own method-specific financial interpretation.

links.label: Read the demo amount and its limits

sections.title: Payment endpoint
paragraphs: A payment endpoint pairs a machine-readable endpoint-type identifier with its receiving-detail payload. Public endpoints belong to an App ID; publishing or reading those details is discovery, not payment execution.

sections.title: Payment endpoint identifier
paragraphs: The machine-readable name of an endpoint type, such as btc-lightning-bolt11. Its constructor checks structural path safety; the application still needs to support the selected payment method.

links.label: See supported and unsupported endpoint types

sections.title: Payment list
paragraphs: A collection of endpoint identifiers and their payloads, represented by the library as a map. Public discovery reads the list for a particular payee and App ID; selecting an entry does not execute a payment.

sections.title: Payment proof
paragraphs: A request-correlated message carrying a payment reference, the app and endpoint type used, and a method-specific proof object. The application or payment adapter must validate the evidence and rail outcome; receiving this message alone does not establish settlement.

sections.title: Payment reference
paragraphs: A payee-visible text value used to correlate a payment with Paykit artifacts. Request terms supply it and Payment Proof messages copy it; construction rejects empty, overlong or control-character-containing references.

links.label: See the order reference in request terms

sections.title: Payment request
paragraphs: A payee-initiated private proposal asking a payer to pay according to supplied terms. It combines request and event identifiers with those terms and is sent over an Encrypted Link; low-level callers must enforce sender roles. It coordinates the request, not the financial execution.

sections.title: Payment Request ID
paragraphs: The UUID-v4 identifier for one request, distinct from each lifecycle message's Event ID. Keep it with the counterparty and exact terms when using the SDK's idempotent proposal API; the ID alone does not preserve deduplication after the supporting history is lost.

sections.title: Payment request terms
paragraphs: The payee's requested amount, payment reference and accepted endpoint types, with optional constraints such as recurrence or an endpoint binding. Complete terms must pass builder validation; bound endpoints require a payee App ID and forbid fallback outside the supplied endpoint map.

sections.title: Private application message
paragraphs: A message received over an Encrypted Link, exposed to low-level callers as plaintext with optional version, kind and app-attribution fields. Its Debug formatter redacts the raw body, but the application still holds sensitive plaintext and must keep it out of logs.

links.label: Protect private messages in application memory and logs

sections.title: Private payment list
paragraphs: An app-attributed, versioned message carrying the complete desired endpoint map to a counterparty over an established Encrypted Link, not a patch. SDK private resolution uses private lists and private adapter callbacks only; a missing or stale list does not trigger public fallback.

links.label: Keep private resolution and public discovery separate

sections.title: ProofSubmitted
paragraphs: The SDK request state indicating that a one-time Payment Proof is present in local history. It can be derived while that proof is still queued, so it establishes neither peer receipt nor verified settlement.

sections.title: Pubky session provider
paragraphs: The application or binding boundary that supplies current live Pubky access to the SDK. Session creation, persistence, capability renewal and identity-wide key distribution remain caller responsibilities; a provider returning no live access does not itself sign the SDK out.

links.label: Supply live access without confusing it with sign-in

sections.title: Receipt delivery status
paragraphs: The SDK issuance view tracks delivery of Receipt Access, the message that lets a counterparty retrieve and decrypt an encrypted receipt: locally queued, published (AccessSent), or stopped without automatic retry (AccessFailed). Sent and failed statuses are derived from the matching outbound message while the durable issuance record remains AccessQueued; a retryable delivery error can leave the view queued with an error. Publication is not proof that the peer read the receipt or that payment settled.

links.label: Interpret receipt delivery separately from settlement

sections.title: Shared state
paragraphs: The one logical SDK state backing that apps sharing a Pubky identity must use for their private coordination. PubkySharedStateStorage encrypts this state, but requires independently verified Homeserver 0.16.2 or newer with GCS storage and correctly locked writers. Encryption does not hide resource existence, size or update timing, or prevent homeserver replay.

sections.title: Storage adapter
paragraphs: The SDK's application-supplied boundary for its authoritative logical state. It must provide atomic transactions and stable outbound/private-stream ordering, with the same logical backing for apps on one identity. Each transaction is atomic, but a later error does not undo earlier commits; a storage operation must not call SDK methods or wait for tasks using that same storage.

sourceLinks.label: Receipt issuance and derived delivery states

pages.title: Resources
pages.description: Version-pinned upstream reading for choosing an integration layer and checking application responsibilities.

sections.title: Start with the protocol overview
paragraphs: The repository overview explains public and private payment discovery, core vocabulary and the division between Paykit and application code. Read it first for protocol context before choosing an integration layer.

sections.title: Use the stateless Rust library
paragraphs: The library README covers stateless Rust protocol helpers and caller-owned Pubky sessions, keys and timeouts. For this RC9 snapshot, check your dependency pin rather than copying the README's 0.1.0 quick-start dependency.

sections.title: Plan a stateful Rust integration
paragraphs: The SDK README introduces durable state, shared-identity coordination and the storage, live-session and payment-adapter boundaries. Use it when planning a stateful Rust integration; payment execution and settlement detection remain application or adapter responsibilities.

sections.title: Explore the mobile binding surface
paragraphs: The FFI README covers Swift/Kotlin SDK bindings, platform callbacks and mobile workflows. Use its build and initialization sections when planning a mobile integration.

sections.title: Consult the official integration skill
paragraphs: The official upstream integration skill outlines shared-identity setup and application-owned payment responsibilities. Read this pinned original alongside your dependency pin; its internal branch links are navigation aids, not release guarantees.

sections.title: Check shared-state deployment constraints
paragraphs: The storage contract sets out homeserver and GCS prerequisites, locked-writer rules and encryption limits for shared identity state. Read it before multi-app deployment; Paykit does not automatically check the server version or backend.

sections.title: Compare the snapshot's change history
paragraphs: Use the pinned changelog to compare recorded changes when planning an update. Read its Unreleased section as snapshot notes, not a promise that every entry is a separately shipped release.
